court: In the High Court of Madras
case_number: WP No. 3725 of 2026 and W.M.P. No. 4138 of 2026
advocates: For Petitioner(s): Mr. R. Chandra Sudan
For Respondent(s): Mr. U. Baranidharan, Special Government Pleader for R 1 and R 2
prayer: PRAYER: Writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, pleased to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the 2nd respondent to entertain and accept the posthumous registration of the will dated 2.11.2016 executed by the testator Late. K. Kalimuthu in favour of the petitioners in accordance with the provisions of the Registration Act, 1908 in time bound manner.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, J.:— The petitioners assert that they are the legatees under Will dated 02.11.2016 executed by the deceased father of the first petitioner and the deceased husband of the second petitioner. Upon being orally informed that the Will will not be received for registration, the present writ petition has been filed.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner referred to a check slip issued on 03.11.2016 informing the testator that the parent document should be produced for purposes of registration.

3. Mr. U. Baranidharan, learned Special Government Pleader, accepts notice for respondents 1 and 2. He submits that an inquiry would be held before a decision is taken. The petitioners have filed a copy of Will dated 02.11.2016. The death certificate of the testator is on record and indicates that he died on 10.11.2016. Therefore, it is clear that the testator died within a few days of the execution of the Will. The petitioner has arrayed the sister of the first petitioner as the third respondent. It also becomes necessary to verify whether the Will was challenged by the third respondent and, if so, whether orders were issued in relation thereto by a Competent Court. Nonetheless, the petitioner is correct in stating that a Will may be presented for registration posthumously under Section 41 of the Registration Act. Therefore, re-consideration is necessary.

4. Accordingly, the petitioners are permitted to re-present the Will for registration before the registering officer within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. Upon such re-presentation, the registering officer shall issue notice to the petitioners, third respondent herein and any other Class-1 legal heir of the testator and thereafter either register the Will or issue a speaking order of refusal. These actions shall be undertaken within thirty days from the date of re-presentation.

5. This writ petition is disposed of on the above terms. No costs. Consequently, the connected writ miscellaneous petition is ordered.
